verses.zh: 你们要称谢耶和华，因他本为善；他的慈爱永远长存！
verses.en: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good,and his loyal love endures.[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 107. The psalmist praises God for his kindness to his exiled people.

verses.zh: 愿耶和华的赎民说这话，就是他从敌人手中所救赎的，
verses.en: Let those delivered by the Lord speak out,[NOTE:1] those whom he delivered[NOTE:2] from the power[NOTE:3] of the enemy
notes: Heb “for forever [is] his loyal love.”
Or “let the redeemed of the Lord say [so].”
Or “redeemed.”

verses.zh: 从各地，从东从西，从南从北，所招聚来的。
verses.en: and gathered from foreign lands,[NOTE:1] from east and west,from north and south.
notes: Heb “hand.”

verses.zh: 他们在旷野荒地漂流，寻不见可住的城邑，
verses.en: They wandered through the wilderness, in a wasteland;[NOTE:1] they found no road to a city in which to live.
notes: Heb “from lands.” The word “foreign” is supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 又饥又渴，心里发昏。
verses.en: They were hungry and thirsty;they fainted from exhaustion.[NOTE:1]
notes: The MT divides the verse so the line ends “on a wasteland of a road.” The LXX divides the line before “road” as in the translation.

verses.zh: 于是，他们在苦难中哀求耶和华；他从他们的祸患中搭救他们，
verses.en: They cried out to the Lord in their distress;he delivered them from their troubles.

verses.zh: 又领他们行走直路，使他们往可居住的城邑。
verses.en: He led them on a level road[NOTE:1] that they might find a city in which to live.
notes: Heb “and their soul in them fainted.”

verses.zh: 但愿人因耶和华的慈爱和他向人所行的奇事都称赞他；
verses.en: Let them give thanks to the Lord for his loyal loveand for the amazing things he has done for people.[NOTE:1]
notes: A level road. See Jer 31:9.

verses.zh: 因他使心里渴慕的人得以知足，使心里饥饿的人得饱美物。
verses.en: For he has satisfied those who thirst,[NOTE:1] and those who hunger he has filled with food.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and [for] his amazing deeds for the sons of man.”

Heb “[the] longing throat.” The noun נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh), which frequently refers to one’s very being or soul, here probably refers to one’s parched “throat” (note the parallelism with נֶפֶשׁ רְעֵבָה, nefesh reʿevah, “hungry throat”).

verses.zh: 那些坐在黑暗中、死荫里的人被困苦和铁链捆锁，
verses.en: They sat in utter darkness,[NOTE:1] bound in painful iron chains[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and [the] hungry throat he has filled [with] good.”

Heb “those who sat in darkness and deep darkness.” Synonyms are joined here to emphasize the degree of “darkness” experienced by the exiles. The Hebrew term צַלְמָוֶת (tsalmavet, “deep darkness”) has traditionally been understood as a compound noun, meaning “shadow of death” (צֵל + מָוֶת [tsel + mavet]; see BDB 853 s.v. צַלְמָוֶת; cf. NASB). Other authorities prefer to vocalize the form צַלְמוּת (tsalmut) and understand it as an abstract noun (from the root צלם) meaning “darkness.” An examination of the word’s usage favors the latter derivation. It is frequently associated with darkness/night and contrasted with light/morning (see Job 3:5; 10:21-22; 12:22; 24:17; 28:3; 34:22; Ps 107:10, 14; Isa 9:1; Jer 13:16; Amos 5:8). In some cases the darkness described is associated with the realm of death (Job 10:21-22; 38:17), but this is a metaphorical application of the word and does not reflect its inherent meaning. In Ps 107:10 the word refers metonymically to a dungeon, which in turn metaphorically depicts the place of Israel’s exile (see vv. 2-3).

verses.zh: 是因他们违背　神的话语，藐视至高者的旨意。
verses.en: because they had rebelled against God’s commands[NOTE:1] and rejected the instructions of the Most High.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “those bound in suffering and iron.” “Suffering and iron” is a hendiadys (like English “good and angry”), where both words contribute to one idea. In this case the first word characterizes the second; the iron (chains) contribute to the prisoners’ pain and suffering.
Heb “the words of God.”

verses.zh: 所以，他用劳苦治服他们的心；他们仆倒，无人扶助。
verses.en: So he used suffering to humble them;[NOTE:1] they stumbled and no one helped them up.
notes: The divine title “Most High” (עֶלְיוֹן ʿelyon) pictures God as the exalted ruler of the universe who vindicates the innocent and judges the wicked. See especially Pss 7:17; 9:2; 18:13; 21:7; 47:2.

verses.zh: 于是，他们在苦难中哀求耶和华；他从他们的祸患中拯救他们。
verses.en: They cried out to the Lord in their distress;he delivered them from their troubles.

verses.zh: 他从黑暗中和死荫里领他们出来，折断他们的绑索。
verses.en: He brought them out of the utter darkness[NOTE:1] and tore off their shackles.
notes: Heb “and he subdued with suffering their heart.”

verses.zh: 但愿人因耶和华的慈爱和他向人所行的奇事都称赞他；
verses.en: Let them give thanks to the Lord for his loyal loveand for the amazing things he has done for people.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “darkness and deep darkness.” See the note on the word “darkness” in v. 10.

verses.zh: 因为他打破了铜门，砍断了铁闩。
verses.en: For he shattered the bronze gatesand hacked through the iron bars.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and [for] his amazing deeds for the sons of man.” See v. 8.

verses.zh: 愚妄人因自己的过犯和自己的罪孽便受苦楚。
verses.en: They acted like fools in their rebellious ways[NOTE:1] and suffered because of their sins.
notes: The language of v. 16 recalls Isa 45:2.

verses.zh: 他们心里厌恶各样的食物，就临近死门。
verses.en: They lost their appetite for all food,[NOTE:1] and they drew near the gates of death.
notes: Heb “fools [they were] because of the way of their rebellion.”

verses.zh: 于是，他们在苦难中哀求耶和华；他从他们的祸患中拯救他们。
verses.en: They cried out to the Lord in their distress;he delivered them from their troubles.

verses.zh: 他发命医治他们，救他们脱离死亡。
verses.en: He sent them an assuring word[NOTE:1] and healed them;he rescued them from the pits where they were trapped.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “all food their appetite loathed.”
Heb “he sent his word.” This probably refers to an oracle of assurance which announced his intention to intervene (see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 [WBC], 59).

verses.zh: 但愿人因耶和华的慈爱和他向人所行的奇事都称赞他。
verses.en: Let them give thanks to the Lord for his loyal loveand for the amazing things he has done for people.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he rescued from their traps.” The Hebrew word שְׁחִית (shekhit, “trap”) occurs only here and in Lam 4:20, where it refers to a trap or pit in which one is captured. Because of the rarity of the term and the absence of an object with the verb “rescued,” some prefer to emend the text of Ps 107:20, reading מִשַּׁחַת חַיָּתָם (mishakhat khayyatam, “[he rescued] their lives from the pit”). Note also NIV “from the grave,” which interprets the “pit” as Sheol or the grave.

verses.zh: 愿他们以感谢为祭献给他，欢呼述说他的作为！
verses.en: Let them present thank offerings,and loudly proclaim what he has done.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and [for] his amazing deeds for the sons of man.” See v. 8.

verses.zh: 在海上坐船，在大水中经理事务的，
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Some traveled on[NOTE:2] the sea in shipsand carried cargo over the vast waters.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and let them proclaim his works with a ringing cry.”

Verses 23-30, which depict the Lord rescuing sailors from a storm at sea, do not seem to describe the exiles’ situation, unless the word picture is metaphorical. Perhaps the psalmist here broadens his scope and offers an example of God’s kindness to the needy beyond the covenant community.
Heb “those going down [into].”

verses.zh: 他们看见耶和华的作为，并他在深水中的奇事。
verses.en: They witnessed the acts of the Lord,his amazing feats on the deep water.

verses.zh: 因他一吩咐，狂风就起来，海中的波浪也扬起。
verses.en: He gave the order for a windstorm,[NOTE:1] and it stirred up the waves of the sea.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “doers of work on the mighty waters.”
Heb “he spoke and caused to stand a stormy wind.”

verses.zh: 他们上到天空，下到海底；他们的心因患难便消化。
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] reached up to the sky,then dropped into the depths.The sailors’ strength[NOTE:2] left them[NOTE:3] because the danger was so great.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “and it stirred up its [i.e., the sea’s, see v. 23] waves.”
That is, the waves (see v. 25).
Heb “their being”; traditionally “their soul” (referring to that of the sailors). This is sometimes translated “courage” (cf. NIV, NRSV).
Or “melted.”

verses.zh: 他们摇摇晃晃，东倒西歪，好像醉酒的人；他们的智慧无法可施。
verses.en: They swayed[NOTE:1] and staggered like drunks,and all their skill proved ineffective.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “from danger.”
Only here does the Hebrew verb חָגַג (khagag; normally meaning “to celebrate”) carry the nuance “to sway.”

verses.zh: 于是，他们在苦难中哀求耶和华，他从他们的祸患中领出他们来。
verses.en: They cried out to the Lord in their distress;he delivered them from their troubles.

verses.zh: 他使狂风止息，波浪就平静。
verses.en: He calmed the storm,[NOTE:1] and the waves[NOTE:2] grew silent.
notes: The Hitpael of בָּלַע (balaʿ) occurs only here in the OT. Traditionally the form is derived from the verbal root בלע (“to swallow”), but HALOT 135 s.v. III בלע understands a homonym here with the meaning “to be confused.”
Heb “he raised [the] storm to calm.”

verses.zh: 风息浪静，他们便欢喜；他就引他们到所愿去的海口。
verses.en: The sailors[NOTE:1] rejoiced because the waves[NOTE:2] grew quiet,and he led them to the harbor[NOTE:3] they desired.
notes: Heb “their waves.” The antecedent of the third masculine plural pronominal suffix is not readily apparent, unless it refers back to “waters” in v. 23.
Heb “they”; the referent (the sailors) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “they”; the referent (the waves) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 但愿人因耶和华的慈爱和他向人所行的奇事都称赞他。
verses.en: Let them give thanks to the Lord for his loyal loveand for the amazing things he has done for people.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew noun occurs only here in the OT.

verses.zh: 愿他们在民的会中尊崇他，在长老的位上赞美他！
verses.en: Let them exalt him in the assembly of the people.Let them praise him in the place where the leaders preside.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and [for] his amazing deeds for the sons of man.” See v. 8.

verses.zh: 他使江河变为旷野，叫水泉变为干渴之地，
verses.en: He turned[NOTE:1] streams into a desert,springs of water into arid land,
notes: Heb “in the seat of the elders.”

verses.zh: 使肥地变为硷地；这都因其间居民的罪恶。
verses.en: and a fruitful land into a barren place,[NOTE:1] because of the sin of its inhabitants.
notes: The verbal form appears to be a preterite, which is most naturally taken as narrational. (The use of prefixed forms with vav [ו] consecutive in vv. 36-37 favor this.) The psalmist may return to the theme of God’s intervention for the exiles (see vv. 4-22, especially vv. 4-9). However, many regard vv. 33-41 as a hymnic description which generalizes about God’s activities among men. In this case it would be preferable to use the English present tense throughout (cf. NEB, NRSV).

verses.zh: 他使旷野变为水潭，叫旱地变为水泉。
verses.en: As for his people,[NOTE:1] he turned[NOTE:2] a desert into a pool of waterand a dry land into springs of water.
notes: Heb “a salty land.”

The words “As for his people” are not included in the Hebrew text, but have been supplied in the translation for the sake of clarity. The psalmist contrasts God’s judgment on his enemies with his blessing of his people. See the note on the word “enemies” in v. 39 for further discussion.

verses.zh: 他使饥饿的人住在那里，好建造可住的城邑，
verses.en: He allowed the hungry to settle there,and they established a city in which to live.

verses.zh: 又种田地，栽葡萄园，得享所出的土产。
verses.en: They cultivated[NOTE:1] fieldsand planted vineyards,which yielded a harvest of fruit.[NOTE:2]
notes: The verbal form appears to be a preterite, which is most naturally taken as narrational. See the note on the word “turned” in v. 33.
Heb “sowed seed in.”

verses.zh: 他又赐福给他们，叫他们生养众多，也不叫他们的牲畜减少。
verses.en: He blessed[NOTE:1] them so that they became very numerous.He would not allow their cattle to decrease in number.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “fruit [as] produce.”

“Bless” here carries the nuance “endue with sexual potency, make fertile.” See Gen 1:28, where the statement “he blessed them” directly precedes the command “be fruitful and populate the earth” (see also 1:22). The verb “bless” carries this same nuance in Gen 17:16 (where God’s blessing of Sarai imparts to her the capacity to bear a child); 48:16 (where God’s blessing of Joseph’s sons is closely associated with their having numerous descendants); and Deut 7:13 (where God’s blessing is associated with fertility in general, including numerous descendants). See also Gen 49:25 (where Jacob uses the noun derivative in referring to “blessings of the breast and womb,” an obvious reference to fertility) and Gen 27:27 (where the verb is used of a field to which God has given the capacity to produce vegetation).

verses.zh: 他们又因暴虐、患难、愁苦，就减少且卑下。
verses.en: As for their enemies,[NOTE:1] they decreased in number and were beaten down,because of painful distress[NOTE:2] and suffering.
notes: The verbal form in this line appears to be an imperfect, which may be taken as customary (drawing attention to typical action in a past time frame) or as generalizing (in which case one should use the English present tense, understanding a move from narrative to present reality).

The words “As for their enemies” are not included in the Hebrew text, but have been supplied in the translation for the sake of clarity. Without such clarification, one might think that v. 39 refers to those just mentioned in v. 38 as objects of divine blessing, which would contradict the point just emphasized by the psalmist. The structure of vv. 33-42 is paneled (A-B-A-B). In vv. 33-34 the psalmist describes God’s judgment upon his enemies (perhaps those who had enslaved his people). In vv. 35-38 he contrasts this judgment with the divine blessing poured out on God’s people. (See the note on the word “people” in v. 35.) In vv. 39-40 he contrasts this blessing with the judgment experienced by enemies, before returning in vv. 41-42 to the blessing experienced by God’s people.

verses.zh: 他使君王蒙羞被辱，使他们在荒废无路之地漂流。
verses.en: He would pour[NOTE:1] contempt upon princes,and he made them wander in a wasteland with no road.
notes: Heb “from the oppression of calamity.”

verses.zh: 他却将穷乏人安置在高处，脱离苦难，使他的家属多如羊群。
verses.en: Yet he protected[NOTE:1] the needy from oppressionand cared for his families like a flock of sheep.
notes: The active participle is understood as past durative here, drawing attention to typical action in a past time frame. However, it could be taken as generalizing (in which case one should translate using the English present tense), in which case the psalmist moves from narrative to present reality. Perhaps the participial form appears because the statement is lifted from Job 12:21.

verses.zh: 正直人看见就欢喜；罪孽之辈必塞口无言。
verses.en: When the godly see this, they rejoice,and every sinner[NOTE:1] shuts his mouth.
notes: Heb “set on high.”

verses.zh: 凡有智慧的，必在这些事上留心，也必思想耶和华的慈爱。
verses.en: Whoever is wise, let him take note of these things.Let them consider the Lord’s acts of loyal love.
